description: DEDDIAG provides electricity observations from 15 German homes and 50 appliances over periods of up to 3.5 years. The Rosenheim research team records appliances relevant to load shifting, including refrigerators, dishwashers and washing machines, at a temporal resolution of 1 Hz. One home also has three-phase mains observations, and 14 appliances have manually marked start and stop events. Figshare publishes household ZIP packages, documentation and SQL import files under CC BY 4.0 with free access. These observations can calibrate appliance-demand, disaggregation and flexibility models for building energy simulations, complementing data-uk-dale-domestic-appliance-level-electricity. A caveat is that recording periods and available devices differ by home, so the dataset is not a balanced sample of German households. An absence of observed power also needs to be distinguished from interrupted monitoring. The related Python loader and monitoring system have separate software identities and licences. No measurement package was downloaded or imported into a database.
